title: VPC Install Readiness Sweeper — preflight validator for quotas, IAM, DNS, GPU
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Implement a deterministic preflight validator (CLI + Terraform plan-time hook + Console preview) that verifies readiness for Redwood Private (VPC) installs. This ticket covers both the IaC integration points and the runtime checks we run before committing a Private install.

Scope and motivation:
- Reduce failed customer installs caused by common environment issues (quotas, misconfigured IAM, DNS mismatch, GPU capacity shortages).
- Provide actionable remediation guidance so SRE/SE teams and customers can fix infra before running automated installers.
- Surface clear failure codes and metrics to the Console and our support stack to shorten time-to-resolution.

Checks to run (priority order and behavior):
1) Service Quotas (soft-fail vs hard-fail): verify cloud-provider quotas that commonly block installs. Examples: EC2 vCPU/GPU quota, ENI quota, EIP quota, VPC peering limits, subnet IP address counts, NAT gateway limits. By default, failures are soft if there is an automatic quota increase route (we show guidance). For quotas that cannot be increased automatically (account limits), the check fails hard.
2) IAM and SCPs: validate role/trust policies and permissions required for the installer and runtime agents. Confirm that the supplied cross-account role or service principal can create/attach ENIs, manage SG rules, create IAM roles, put/get KMS keys, and list EC2 instance types. Also detect organization SCPs and deny policies that would block key actions.
3) DNS and Private Hosted Zones: confirm that DNS records required for service discovery (control-plane endpoints, registry, internal load balancers) will resolve from the install VPC. Test forward and reverse lookup, VPC resolver rules, and if using AWS PrivateLink, validate interface endpoint service names and subnets.
4) GPU capacity forecast: query cloud provider placement APIs and internal capacity map to assert sufficient GPU capacity of the requested instance families in the chosen AZs/region. For reservations/reserved capacity customers, confirm reserved pool is usable by the account and not attributed elsewhere. Report ETA if immediate capacity unavailable (e.g., vendor capacity replenishment windows).
5) Network reachability and quotas: check that required outbound/inbound ports can be opened in the VPC and that NAT/egress patterns satisfy service needs. Validate public/private subnet segmentation and that control-plane endpoints are routable.
6) KMS/HSM and secrets: ensure the KMS key ARN is accessible and that key policy allows the Redwood installer principal to encrypt/decrypt. If HSM is requested, validate attestation and required drivers.

Integration points and UX:
- Terraform module hooks: add a preflight data source (redwood_private_preflight) that can be invoked in a plan to show pass/fail per-check and a remediation block. The data source returns human-friendly strings and standardized exit codes.
- CLI mode: redwoodctl preflight --manifest ./deploy.yaml returns JSON exit codes and a text summary. Exit codes mapped to Console display: 0=OK, 10=soft-fail, 20=hard-fail, 30=unreachable/service-error.
- Console: a "Preflight report" UI that renders the checks, severity, and one-click remediation links (open quota request form, sample IAM policy, DNS verification steps).

Failure semantics and tolerance:
- Soft-fail: recommended to fix but installer can continue with explicit --force flag. Examples: subnet IP low, quota close to threshold with auto-increase path.
- Hard-fail: blocks installer by default; requires manual remediation and re-run. Examples: missing iam:PassRole, SCP deny for EC2, irrecoverable GPU zero-capacity with no ETA.

Telemetry and observability:
- Emit metrics per-check outcome (preflight.check.<name>.result = OK|SOFT_FAIL|HARD_FAIL) with tags for region/az/account-id and installer version.
- Attach run_id to Console/Support so we can replay server-side checks for debugging.
- Log samples of API responses (sanitized) to an internal S3 bucket for support debugability.

Acceptance criteria (see below) and rollout plan are included. Implementation should be modular to allow future cloud providers or on-prem validators.

Notes on trade-offs:
- We will prioritize AWS for the first pass. Azure/GCP follow-ups will reuse the validator framework but require provider-specific quota/placement APIs.
- We intentionally avoid attempting live capacity reservations in preflight to prevent accidental resource consumption. Instead we query placement/availability endpoints and our internal seat map.

Security: Preflight will not store customer secrets. Any credential use is ephemeral and scrubbed from logs. KMS access checks are performed via allowed read-only operations.
